principle: Treat solver-resolution convergence and stencil convergence as separate axes.

separate_future_questions.Q1: Is the historical 0.02 external-gap qualification policy empirically conservative or necessary for reliable rank1 association/curvature?
separate_future_questions.Q2: Are the finite-difference Berry-curvature estimates themselves sufficiently converged in h?
separate_future_questions.separation_rule: Q1 requires an external-gap qualification study; Q2 requires independent h-convergence evidence. Neither question is answered by the other metric.

solver_resolution_axis.request_count_basis: Eight current samples times nine point locations at one new resolution gives 72 logical demands; the two exact cross-sample duplicate relations reduce this to 70 unique requests.
solver_resolution_axis.scientific_reason: Existing control-2 and outer-boundary sequences contain R128 overshoots, so three points do not establish the next-resolution behavior at fixed h.

stencil_axis.request_count_basis: Eight current samples times three fixed resolutions times four new off-center points; the center is reused and no current canonical point is assumed to match.
stencil_axis.scientific_reason: Two stencil values provide one interval difference and cannot test convergence or distinguish cancellation from a finite-stencil limit.
